message.content:
**Short answer:**  
Yes – you can file a noise‑complaint with the City of Atlanta. The city’s noise ordinance is enforced by the Atlanta Police Department (APD) and the City’s Code Enforcement Office, and complaints can be submitted through several channels.

---

## 1. How to file a noise complaint in Atlanta

| Method | What to do | Where to go |
|--------|------------|-------------|
| **Online** | Use the City of Atlanta’s “Noise Complaint” portal. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> (search “noise complaint”) |
| **Phone** | Call 311 (or 404‑656‑3111 if you’re outside the city). | 311 (within Atlanta) |
| **In‑person** | Visit the City Hall or a local police precinct. | City Hall, 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 |
| **Mail** | Send a written complaint to the City’s Code Enforcement Office. | 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 |

### What information you’ll need
- **Date & time** of the disturbance  
- **Location** (address or intersection)  
- **Description** of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs)  
- **Name & contact info** (optional but helpful)  

---

## 2. The legal framework

| Authority | Key points |
|-----------|------------|
| **Georgia State Law** | Georgia’s “Noise Control Act” (O.C.G.A. § 14‑1‑1 et seq.) gives municipalities the power to regulate noise. |
| **City of Atlanta Ordinance** | *Noise Ordinance* (City Code § 10‑1‑1 et seq.) sets acceptable decibel limits and defines prohibited activities. |
| **Enforcement** | Violations can result in citations, fines, or civil action. The city may also refer cases to the APD for immediate enforcement. |

---

## 3. What happens after you file

1. **Acknowledgment** – You’ll receive a confirmation number.  
2. **Investigation** – APD or Code Enforcement will assess the complaint.  
3. **Action** – Depending on severity, they may issue a warning, citation, or order the offending party to cease the activity.  
4. **Follow‑up** – If the noise continues, you can request a repeat inspection or escalation to the City Council.

---

## 4. Tips for a successful complaint

- **Be specific** – Exact times, dates, and descriptions help investigators locate the source.  
- **Record evidence** – If possible, take a short audio clip or note the decibel level (many smartphones have decibel meters).  
- **Check the schedule** – Some areas have “quiet hours” (e.g., 10 p.m.–7 a.m.). Make sure the complaint falls outside those windows.  
- **Follow up** – If you don’t hear back within a week, call 311 to check status.

---

## 5. Quick links

- **Atlanta Noise Ordinance (PDF)** – <https://www.atlantaga.gov/sites/default/files/2024-02/Noise%20Ordinance.pdf>  
- **311 Online Portal** – <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311>  
- **Atlanta Police Department** – <https://www.atlantaga.gov/department/atlantapolice>  
- **City Code Enforcement** – <https://www.atlantaga.gov/department/code-enforcement>  

---

### Bottom line
If you’re experiencing excessive noise in Atlanta, you can—and should—report it to the city. The city’s noise ordinance gives the local council (via the police and code enforcement) the authority to investigate and enforce against violators. Just use one of the channels above, provide clear details, and the city will take it from there.
